question.problem: Given the ellipsoid $(x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}+\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{3}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the ellipsoid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}+\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ (z+2)^{2} & =3(1-(x-1)^{2}-(y-1)^{2}) \\ z+2 & =\pm \sqrt{3(1-(x-1)^{2}-(y-1)^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-(x-1)^{2}-(y-1)^{2}\ge 0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the interior of the circle $(x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}=1$ and its boundary.

Therefore, the domain is 

$$
\{(x,y)\,:\,(x-1)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}\le 1\}.
$$
